conbody.p: A task section is recognized by an imperative heading such as "Install the Driver" or "Replace the Toner Cartridge," paired with an ordered list (<ol>) as the primary body structure. Both signals must be present. An imperative heading without an <ol>, or an <ol> without an imperative heading, does not reliably trigger task classification.
When these signals align, the converter generates a:

ul.li: The opening paragraph maps to both <shortdesc> and <context>.
Each <li> in the primary <ol> maps to <step><cmd>.
A <ul> list or introductory paragraph appearing before the first <ol> maps to <prereq>. A paragraph or second <ol> appearing after the final step maps to <postreq>.

A nested <ol> inside a <li> maps to <substeps>, with each nested <li> mapping to <substep><cmd>.
A nested <ul> inside a <li> maps to <info><ul> as supporting information unless the items are short and mutually exclusive, in which case it maps to <choices>.
